title: How work runs: batches, dispatch, reviews, rulings

entries.summary: Merge fast-forward only, from the CLI, after aggregating the branch into clean logical commits. No merge commits, no GitHub squash merges.
body: Aggregate with `git reset --soft $(git merge-base main HEAD)` and recommit in one to five Conventional Commits when interactive rebase is not available.
The project skill `finishing-a-feature` is the procedure.

entries.summary: No commit that lands on main may fail the ci.yml checked in beside it; sequence a migration's deletions or collapse the red range at aggregation.
body: A fast-forward merge lands every aggregated commit on main; a bisect, a revert target, or a checkout of any of them must build and pass the CI definition at that same commit.

Batch 20 T3: the corpus deletion commits satisfied the cargo-side flip-with-deletion rule at every commit, but the still-present JS gate (corpus.test.mjs) was red from the first deletion commit until the vitest layer itself retired - caught only by the reviewer's per-commit reproduction, and repaired at aggregation by collapsing the range into the deletion commit.

The check at aggregation time: for each collapsed commit, the gates its own ci.yml names run green; a migration that cannot keep an interim gate green retires that gate's subject in the same collapsed commit.

source.ref: batch 20 branch review; task-3-review.json important finding 1; T3 report concerns[10]

entries.summary: Before a new gate or pipeline step ships, walk every commit author class and every generated resource it touches through it on paper; state each accepted red.
body: Batch 24 shipped a payload-stamp mechanism (tree gate + per-commit co-change + range co-change) proven against 40 human-authored commits, while release-please-config.json's own extra-files entry scheduled a bot commit to template/** that trips all three, plus the dogfood version-stamp test -- discovered only at the branch review.

The walk is cheap: enumerate the automation that writes commits to this repository (release-please, Dependabot, the restamp step), list the exact files each writes, and run the new check's predicate against those file sets.

Extended 2026-09-13 (owner, design.md 5.78): the walk covers generated RESOURCES too -- releases, tags, PRs -- with one named owner per resource. The T2 create-collision (design.md 5.77) was two automations both creating the v0.3.0 release object; the commit-class walk alone missed it the same day this rule shipped.

source.ref: batch 24 branch review issues 1-2; adopted standing at the batch-24 report (design.md 5.75)

entries.summary: Every batch measures its token and time cost per phase and per dispatch, so later process changes can be compared with batch 33.
body: Keep `<workspace>/efficiency-windows.json` current: one window (`phase`, `start`, `end`, UTC) per phase: spec, plan, each task wave with its reviews and fix rounds, the live run, and the branch review.

Run `python3 -I .superpowers/sdd/2026-10-10-batch-33/efficiency.py <workspace>` at each phase end and save the output as `<workspace>/efficiency.json`. It sums the controller's model usage (main-session assistant messages, each message id once) and the subagent dispatches that finished in each window (tokens, tool uses, duration), plus wall-clock time.
Record every dispatch's tokens, tool uses, and duration from its completion notification in the ledger row that closes it.

The baseline is batch 33, the first full-tier batch measured this way, and `efficiency-baseline.json` (every dispatch of batches 28 to 33 that the transcripts hold; a dispatch whose call the transcripts lost has no role). Compare a later batch per phase and per dispatch with it, never as one total.

entries.summary: A critical task gets the spec's cases as tests before any code, one RED run at BASE, the whole suite green at HEAD, and one review with no re-review.
body: Owner ruling 2026-10-20 (design.md 173), in place of the purged full tier. A critical task changes the CLI's commands, flags, or output, a schema, authentication or security code, or the data on disk of an install.

The plan writes the spec's cases for the task as tests. The implementer commits them first and records one run that shows them failing at BASE, then makes them pass. The implementer still works test-first for every further change (`process.tdd`); only the evidence shrinks: that RED run and the whole suite passing at HEAD, with no recorded per-step RED and GREEN and no disclosed-mutation proof.

One task review on opus, never a re-review. The controller checks each fix by re-running the reviewer's own reproduction and records it in the ledger (`process.fix-round-verification-record`). A Critical or Important finding goes to a fresh implementer; the controller fixes a Minor one itself.

entries.summary: No batch or task runs a full tier, and nothing escalates to one; work runs the light or the standard tier.
body: Owner ruling 2026-10-20 (design.md 172): "Purge the full tier completely for us as well as for the reference workflow. Instead, for critical tasks, find other a different, faster, more efficient way to assert quality and correctness."
From batch 33's Task 9 on, this repository runs the standard tier: one task review, at most one re-review, and a branch review on opus for a batch of two or more tasks.
The controller fixes a small Minor finding itself and closes it with a verification note (`process.fix-round-verification-record`), instead of dispatching a fix round for it.

The kit's `process.risk-tiers` and the orchestrating skill name a full tier; in this repository this entry wins over them (HR-198 removes the kit's full tier). A critical task runs `process.critical-tasks-test-first` (design.md 173).

entries.summary: Give a fix round to a fresh implementer with the tree state in its brief; a resumed implementer costs about three times the tokens per tool use.
body: Measured in batch 33: Task 5's round 2 on a resumed agent used 732,296 tokens, its round 3 on a fresh agent 163,693; Task 7's round 2c (resumed) used 7,338 tokens per tool use, round 2b (fresh) 2,138.
The brief names FIX_BASE, the findings with the review's own checks, and the controller's positions, so a fresh agent needs no earlier transcript.

source.ref: batch 33 branch review recommendation; progress.md usage rows
